title: Field Trip Vote
story: Your class is voting on a field trip. Each student writes one destination code on a slip: 4 for the aquarium, 9 for the science museum, 17 for the climbing wall, and so on. A trip goes ahead only if one destination gets more than half the votes, and the teacher knows that happened. Which destination won?
task: Write winningTrip(votes). Return the destination code that appears more than votes.length / 2 times.
Such a destination always exists, so there is always exactly one correct answer.
constraints: One value appears more than votes.length / 2 times.

examples.explanation: Five votes, so the winner needs at least 3. The museum, code 9, got 3.
Seven votes, so the winner needs at least 4. Code 17 got exactly 4. The first vote being a 4 does not matter.

hints: With 7 votes, how many does the winner need? Once a destination reaches that, can anything beat it?
You need each destination's vote count so far: a tally sheet with one line per destination.
Which structure keeps a count per code when you do not know in advance which codes will appear?
Walk the votes once with a map from code to count. After each vote, if that count is now more than votes.length / 2, return that code.
bruteForce: For each vote, scan the whole box and count matching slips; return the first code past half. That is O(n²): up to 2.5 billion comparisons for 50,000 votes. Sorting also works, since the winner must fill the middle position, but costs O(n log n) and reorders the slips.

js: * @param {number[]} votes  one destination code per student
* @return {number} the code with more than half the votes

tests.note: winner not first in a row
alternating, winner never twice in a row
first vote is not the winner
winner only appears in the second half
winner bunched at the start, one vote at the end
last vote and middle slip (unsorted) are both losers

js: const count = new Map(); // destination -> votes so far
if (c > votes.length / 2) return v; // nobody can catch up now
return -1; // never reached: a winner always exists
py: if count[v] > len(votes) / 2:  # nobody can catch up now
return -1  # never reached: a winner always exists
walkthrough: Read the slips once, keeping a running tally per destination. The moment one passes half the class, it has won.
Trace [9, 4, 9, 17, 9]. Half of 5 is 2.5, so the winner needs 3.
Compare against the total number of votes, not the number read so far: after one slip, its destination has 100% of the votes read but has not won.

An O(1)-memory trick also works: keep one candidate and a counter. Add 1 when a vote matches the candidate, subtract 1 when it does not, and switch candidate when the counter hits 0. Each losing vote cancels one winning vote, and the winner outnumbers everyone else combined, so it is left standing.
solution.timeWhy: One pass, with O(1) average work per vote for the map update.
solution.spaceWhy: The map holds one entry per different destination, up to about n / 2 of them.
solution.takeaway: To find which value occurs most, or past some threshold, keep a hash map of counts while you walk the list. It replaces one full recount per element with a single update.
